parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the complete Flasky specification: app factory, models, auth/main/API blueprints, templates, tests, migrations, root packaging files, and compatibility with old Flask dependencies.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It wrote the foundation itself and split the remaining work into four subagents: auth, main/templates/static, API, and entry/tests/migrations/root files, with the parent resuming for final verification.
parallel.implementation: Children produced the assigned modules in a shared workspace. The API child had to wait for main to finish; the main child corrected the PageDown helper; the tests child relaxed one API URL comparison after observing relative versus external URLs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent consumed the aggregate AgentSwarm result, listed the final tree, ran unittest and pytest, checked imports and installability, ran node-style examples, and ended by reporting the lack of a submit tool.
parallel.verification: Local verification reached 31 unittest tests OK with one skip, pytest 30 passed with one skip, import checks, pip install verification, and node-example smoke checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The current official evaluation still failed 1 of 34 tests. The mounted data does not expose the hidden failing assertion, so the unresolved product defect cannot be tied to a specific proven concurrency boundary.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same Flasky specification and implemented the complete app surface in one sequential workspace: models, blueprints, templates, API, migrations, tests, packaging, and docs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned all stages end to end, using a todo list late in the process for migrations and final test repair rather than delegating any work to child agents.
serial.implementation: It wrote root files, app package, main/auth/API blueprints, templates, tests, static assets, and generated the migrations skeleton, then iteratively repaired observed failures.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The same actor handled integration as implementation proceeded, generating migrations through flasky.py db init and preserving direct context for later template and API fixes.
serial.verification: It ran pytest, targeted failing tests, inspected itsdangerous signatures, smoke-tested web and API flows, ran final pytest, and ran python flasky.py test before closing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unresolved defect is visible: the current completed evaluation passed all 34 of 34 tests and the serial control contains no delegation or subagents.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full Flasky requirement set from the shared prompt and decomposed the app into foundation plus auth, main, API, tests, migrations, and packaging work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used the same prompt and built the same requirement areas sequentially, including the social features, REST API, tests, installability, and migrations skeleton.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no prompt-level requirement difference; the observed difference appears in later implementation and verification repair rather than initial task interpretation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote core foundation files, then delegated four distinct owned scopes to subagents: auth, main, API, and root/tests/migrations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept ownership centralized in the main actor, writing root files first and then proceeding through app, blueprints, templates, tests, migrations, and fixes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created real concurrent component ownership; serial retained end-to-end ownership. The split itself was coherent enough to avoid a missing owner label.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children coordinated through shared foundation files and later handoffs. Interface friction appeared as a transient incomplete main import and a local API URL assertion mismatch, but the children either waited or adjusted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial encountered dependency and API details directly, inspected itsdangerous signatures, fixed token serialization, and kept the URL/API behavior in one thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more cross-component interface friction, but the evidence shows visible repair and post-join verification rather than an unresolved missing contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced the application through separately written module chunks. Main and API children performed scoped smoke checks; the tests child added a broad local test suite and migration files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all layers in sequence, then corrected specific defects found by tests and manual web/API flows.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel implementation was componentized and locally verified by children; serial implementation was more iterative across the whole integrated app.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four subagents returned an aggregate AgentSwarm result, after which the parent continued with whole-project checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results; the main actor directly carried findings from each test/smoke failure into the next edit.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a join and aggregate handoff step; serial had direct continuity. The join happened before final verification, so there is no missing join or unused completed result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote into one workspace and observed transient incomplete state, such as the API child failing while the main blueprint was not finished, then succeeding after waiting.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated within one actor and used smoke failures on pages and templates to make local edits before final checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-workspace timing friction; serial saw ordinary sequential integration failures. The parallel transient did not leave a directly evidenced unresolved shared-state consequence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran post-join unittest, pytest, import checks, installability checks, and node-style examples; local checks were green after adapting the smoke scripts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran pytest repeatedly, targeted failing tests, verified web/API smoke flows, and finished with both pytest and python flasky.py test green.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified substantially, but serial's iterative failures drove direct product edits through to the official 34/34 result, while parallel's local suite still missed one hidden official case.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished without timeout after the swarm and final checks, then closed by noting no submit tool was available.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also finished without timeout and with remaining budget after final tests and status cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run shows budget exhaustion or cancellation. Parallel used more requests and tokens, but normal higher cost from parallel fan-out is not a retained Load Imbalance pattern.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is serial_only_pass: parallel completed and passed 33 of 34 tests, while serial completed and passed 34 of 34. Parallel created a multi-agent build and ran substantial local integration checks after joining all four children, but one official hidden case remained failing. Serial used one continuous implementation loop and repaired observed runtime/API/template failures before final checks. The mounted evidence supports this as a process and verification contrast, but the exact hidden failing assertion is not available, so no unique root cause is claimed.
parallel_contributors: The parallel build depended on child handoffs and shared workspace integration before parent verification, creating transient API/main and PageDown failures that were later repaired locally.
The tests/root child changed a local API URL assertion to tolerate relative versus external Location behavior, so local green tests may have been less aligned with a hidden official requirement.
serial_contributors: The serial actor kept full context while fixing token serialization, anonymous profile rendering, post template pagination, and API flows.
The serial actor ran final pytest, API smoke checks with roles inserted, and python flasky.py test before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel included authored migration version files while serial generated a migrations skeleton; serial nevertheless passed official evaluation, so this is not a supported explanation for the failure.
Parallel local API verification tolerated an external/relative URL mismatch, while serial's later API smoke verified create, edit, comment, timeline, user posts, and bad request behavior.
evaluator_effects: The mounted official result exposes only aggregate counts, not the hidden failing assertion for the one parallel failure.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
